rows.name: Biomedical signals check
rows.summary: Amplifiers, interference and the safety rules that come before the signal.
questions: An ECG front end uses a differential amplifier mainly to…|increase gain|reject the mains interference common to both electrodes|remove baseline wander|protect the patient|#1
A signal sampled at 250 Hz without an anti-alias filter can be corrupted by…|mains hum|higher-frequency content folding down into the band of interest|electrode drift|quantisation only|#1
Which limit matters most before an electrode touches a patient?|The amplifier bandwidth|Leakage current through the patient|The ADC resolution|The display refresh rate|#1
Baseline wander in an ECG usually comes from…|power line interference|patient movement and respiration|the ADC|aliasing|#1

rows.name: Circuit analysis check
rows.summary: Ohm’s law, series/parallel networks and power.
questions: Two 100 Ω resistors in parallel give a total resistance of…|200 Ω|100 Ω|50 Ω|25 Ω|#2
In a series circuit, which quantity is the same through every component?|Voltage|Current|Power|Resistance|#1
A 12 V supply across 6 Ω dissipates how much power?|2 W|12 W|24 W|72 W|#2
Kirchhoff’s voltage law is a statement of…|charge conservation|energy conservation per loop|Ohm’s law|power factor|#1

rows.name: Feedback control check
rows.summary: Checks understanding of error, feedback and stability.
questions: In a feedback loop, what is the error signal?|Measured output|Setpoint minus measured output|Control output|Disturbance|#1

What does the integral term mainly remove?|Steady-state error|Noise|Nonlinearity|Sensor offset only|#0
Why is derivative action often filtered?|It amplifies measurement noise|It slows the loop|It removes offset|It is not used in practice|#0

rows.name: Data structures check
rows.summary: Complexity intuition and structure choice.

Binary search requires the input to be…|unique|sorted|small|numeric only|#1
Which structure best models a last-in-first-out process?|Queue|Stack|Linked list|Heap|#1
Breadth-first search is implemented using a…|stack|queue|heap|hash map|#1

rows.name: Datums, projections and coordinates check
rows.summary: Reference frames, reprojection and the units a map is really in.
questions: A list of coordinates with no coordinate reference system is…|precise to within one metre|useless, because the numbers could belong to any datum|the same as WGS 84|always latitude and longitude|#1

Reprojecting data from a geographic to a projected coordinate system…|improves its accuracy|changes the coordinates and can change computed distances and areas|always increases precision|drops the attribute fields|#1

A datum and a projection differ in that…|a datum is a reference frame for the Earth and a projection maps it onto a plane|a projection defines the shape of the Earth and a datum flattens it|they are two names for one thing|a projection is always more accurate|#0

A distance measured on a projected map differs from the ground distance because…|the map is wrong|the projection imposes a scale factor that varies with location|the ground moves between measurements|the survey was imprecise|#1

rows.name: GIS analysis and projection pitfalls check

questions: Which question suits a raster data model better than a vector one?|who owns this parcel|how slope varies across a hillside|where the nearest school is|which streets are one-way|#1

A buffer of 0.01 applied in a geographic coordinate system will…|produce a correct 10-metre buffer|produce a buffer whose real size changes with latitude because degrees are not a fixed ground distance|fail immediately with an error|double the number of polygons|#1
A spatial join differs from an attribute join in that it…|is always faster|matches records by their position rather than by a shared key|needs no data cleaning|only works on point layers|#1
The main purpose of a validity or topology check is to…|speed up rendering|find geometry that breaks rules and would corrupt later analysis|convert between formats|simplify polygons for display|#1

rows.name: Lean flow and capacity check

Increasing machine utilisation beyond a point lengthens lead time mainly because…|machines wear faster|queues grow as spare capacity disappears|operators slow down|the schedule changes less often|#1
A buffer between two stations exists to…|increase inventory value|decouple one station’s stoppage from the next|hide defects|keep operators busy|#1

rows.name: Aerospace engineer
rows.summary: Analyses flight vehicles: aerodynamics, structures, propulsion and control.
rows.description: Aerospace work is analysis-heavy and safety-critical. The graph route starts with mathematics, physics and mechanics, then adds aerodynamics and structural considerations; simulation is the practical entry point for students without workshop access.
responsibilities: Model aerodynamic forces and flight behaviour
Check structural margins under load cases
Validate models against wind-tunnel or flight data
Document assumptions and safety margins
portfolioIdeas: A wing-section analysis comparing two theories against published data
A flight-simulator model with stability analysis
A lightweight structural design with a margin-of-safety table
assumptions: Regulated industry: this route builds fundamentals and analysis skill, not certification.

rows.name: AI and machine learning engineer
rows.summary: Trains, evaluates and deploys models that make predictions or generate content.
rows.description: Machine learning engineers sit between data science and software engineering: they prepare data, train and evaluate models, then ship them behind an API with monitoring. Mathematics, statistics and solid programming are prerequisites; the graph insists on statistics and data handling before model training for a reason.
responsibilities: Prepare and validate datasets for training and evaluation
Train, tune and evaluate models against a baseline
Deploy models behind an API and monitor their behaviour
Document limitations, bias and failure modes honestly
portfolioIdeas: An end-to-end prediction service with a documented evaluation
A reproducible notebook-to-API pipeline for a public dataset
A comparison of two models with an honest error analysis
assumptions: Much entry-level work is data engineering and evaluation, not novel model research.
GPU access can be a practical barrier; free tiers exist but are limited and may change.

rows.name: Biomedical engineer
rows.summary: Designs and proves out devices and instruments that touch patients — hardware, software, materials and paperwork.
rows.description: Biomedical engineers sit between engineering and clinical practice. The work ranges from signal conditioning on an ECG front end, through biomechanics of joints and gait, to the risk file and quality system evidence that lets a device be sold at all. The distinguishing constraint is that the failure mode is a person, so verification, traceability and human factors are part of the engineering rather than an afterthought.
responsibilities: Turn a clinical need into requirements that can be verified
Design or specify instrumentation, implants or assistive devices
Run verification and validation activities and record the evidence
Maintain a risk management file through design changes
portfolioIdeas: An analysis notebook of a public physiological dataset (ECG or gait) with the processing steps written down
A design and risk file for a simple assistive device, including its intended use and its known limitations
A musculoskeletal model of one movement, with the assumptions and their effect on the result stated
assumptions: Clinical roles and device regulation differ by country; this graph covers the engineering foundations and the general regulatory shape, not a specific national approval path.
Patient-facing work almost always requires institutional approvals and supervision that no self-study path can provide.

rows.name: Chemical and process engineer
rows.summary: Turns a laboratory recipe into a plant that runs safely, at scale, at a cost that works.
rows.description: Chemical and process engineers size and tune the equipment that turns raw materials into products: reactors, pumps, heat exchangers, distillation columns and the control loops holding it all steady. The daily work is balances and specifications — how much goes in, how much comes out, at what temperature and pressure — and then the safety case for what happens when it goes wrong. The graph route runs from balances and thermodynamics through transport, reactors and separations to a simulated, safety-checked flowsheet.
responsibilities: Close mass and energy balances around single units and whole flowsheets
Size and specify equipment, then check it against a written design basis
Read and write P&IDs and instrument specifications with the controls team
Run and document hazard studies such as HAZOP, and follow the actions through
portfolioIdeas: A simulated flowsheet of a real process with a closed mass balance and a written design basis
A heat-exchanger sizing workbook that reproduces a worked example within a stated tolerance
A deviation table from a small hazard study, with the safeguards it produced and their limits
assumptions: Job titles, chartership routes and typical pay vary widely by country; this graph describes common foundations, not a hiring bar.
Most entry roles expect chemistry and mathematics to coursework level; this graph does not replace an accredited degree where an employer requires one.

rows.name: Civil and structural engineer
rows.summary: Designs structures and infrastructure that must not fail.
rows.description: Civil engineers work with forces, materials and codes: loads, beams, frames, foundations, water and transport. Safety factors and conservative design are the culture, not an afterthought.
responsibilities: Calculate load paths and member sizes
Check designs against applicable standards and safety factors
Coordinate drawings, quantities and site realities
Inspect and document as-built conditions
portfolioIdeas: A truss or beam design with load calculations and a software cross-check
A small structure model tested physically or in simulation
A site-study report with measurements and photographs
assumptions: Professional practice is regulated; this route builds foundations, not a licence.
Structural software is expensive; free educational tools and hand calculations cover the fundamentals.

rows.name: Cloud and DevOps engineer
rows.summary: Automates building, deploying and operating software, and keeps it observable.
rows.description: Cloud and DevOps engineers make delivery repeatable: version control, CI/CD, containers, infrastructure as code, monitoring and incident response. Linux and scripting are the prerequisites most beginners skip.
responsibilities: Automate build, test and deployment pipelines
Manage infrastructure declaratively and review changes
Monitor services and respond to alerts
Reduce toil and document runbooks
portfolioIdeas: A repository that builds, tests and deploys itself on push with documented stages
A containerised application with health checks and backups
A monitoring stack with a dashboard and one written incident review
assumptions: Free tiers of cloud providers change frequently; most of this route can be practised locally with containers.

rows.name: Cybersecurity analyst
rows.summary: Defends systems: monitoring, vulnerability work, incident response and secure configuration.
rows.description: Security analysts combine networking, operating systems and scripting with an adversarial mindset. The work includes monitoring alerts, hardening systems, testing your own controls lawfully, and responding when something goes wrong. Ethics and authorisation are prerequisites, not optional extras.
responsibilities: Monitor logs and alerts, and triage what matters
Perform authorised vulnerability assessment and hardening
Support incident response and write it up afterwards
Explain risk in plain language to people who own the system
portfolioIdeas: A home lab with documented hardening and monitoring
A write-up of a deliberately vulnerable training application (Juice Shop, WebGoat) with fixes
An analysis of a public breach report and the controls that would have helped
assumptions: Never test systems you do not own or have written permission to test; the portfolio only ever uses deliberately vulnerable targets.
Free-tier lab environments are limited; a local virtual lab is usually more practical.

rows.name: Data scientist and analyst
rows.summary: Turns messy data into decisions using statistics, SQL and clear communication.
rows.description: Data roles start with questions, not models. You collect and clean data, query it with SQL, analyse it statistically, visualise it, and explain what it does and does not show. Strong analysts are usually better communicators than modellers.
responsibilities: Write SQL and scripts to extract and clean data
Run descriptive and inferential analyses
Build dashboards and write up findings for non-technical readers
State uncertainty and data-quality problems explicitly
portfolioIdeas: A cleaned, reproducible analysis of an open dataset
A dashboard that answers three concrete questions
A written report that names its own limitations
assumptions: Job titles vary widely; some analyst roles focus almost entirely on SQL and reporting.

rows.name: Electrical and electronics engineer
rows.summary: Designs circuits, power systems and electronic products.
rows.description: Electrical and electronics engineers analyse circuits, choose components, design boards and deal with power, noise and safety. The graph route goes from fundamentals through circuit analysis and digital logic to a designed, tested board.
responsibilities: Analyse and simulate circuits before building them
Select components against real tolerances and datasheets
Design and test prototypes, including test points and measurement plans
Respect electrical safety limits and standards
portfolioIdeas: A microcontroller board with a schematic, PCB and measurement log
A power supply design with ripple and thermal measurements
A sensor interface board with noise analysis
assumptions: Some projects need lab equipment; simulation and low-voltage work can cover much of the route first.

rows.name: Embedded systems and IoT engineer
rows.summary: Writes firmware for devices that sense, communicate and must run reliably for years.
rows.description: Embedded engineers work close to hardware with constrained memory and real-time requirements. The graph connects electronics fundamentals, programming in C, microcontroller peripherals, connectivity and power budgets.
responsibilities: Write and debug firmware for microcontrollers
Interface sensors over I²C/SPI/UART and handle timing
Design power budgets and low-power modes
Design and test connectivity and over-the-air update paths
portfolioIdeas: A sensor node that logs data reliably for a week
A device with a documented communication protocol and error handling
A low-power build with measured current draw
assumptions: Hardware availability varies by region; simulation and ESP32/Arduino-class boards keep costs low.

rows.name: Industrial and manufacturing engineer
rows.summary: Makes a production system faster, cheaper and more reliable without making it fragile or unsafe.
rows.description: Industrial and manufacturing engineers work on the system rather than the part: how work flows, where the queue forms, which measurements actually control quality, what a machine can do unattended and what a person can reasonably do all shift. The toolkit is statistics, layout, automation and time — and the constraint is always that the line must keep running while you change it.
responsibilities: Measure and improve throughput, quality and cost on an existing process
Design or rebalance a line, cell or service process
Specify automation and the safety interlocks around it
Run investigations when quality or output drifts, and fix the cause rather than the symptom
portfolioIdeas: A control-chart study on a real dataset, including the out-of-control signals and what caused them
A line-balance and layout proposal with the takt time, bottlenecks and staffing it implies
A simulated PLC interlock with a written safety rationale and a table of failure modes
assumptions: Titles vary: continuous improvement engineer, production engineer and operations analyst describe overlapping work, and industries differ enormously in what they expect.
Most improvement work needs shop-floor access and the trust of the people doing the work; no portfolio can substitute for that.

rows.name: Mechanical design engineer
rows.summary: Designs parts and assemblies in CAD and proves they will survive real loads.
rows.description: Mechanical design engineers move between CAD models, hand calculations and manufacturing constraints. The graph route starts with mechanics and materials, then adds CAD, tolerances and design-for-manufacture.
responsibilities: Create and revise 3D models and manufacturing drawings
Check stress, deflection and thermal behaviour against requirements
Choose materials and processes with cost and lead time in mind
Work with machinists and suppliers to fix what the drawing missed
portfolioIdeas: A fully dimensioned drawing set for a working mechanism
A design study with stress calculations and a simulation cross-check
A 3D-printed part redesigned for manufacturability with tolerance notes
assumptions: Commercial CAD licences are expensive; the route below uses FreeCAD and OnShape’s free plan for education.

rows.name: Renewable energy engineer
rows.summary: Designs and evaluates solar, wind, storage and efficiency systems.
rows.description: Renewable energy engineers size systems, model energy flows, and weigh cost, reliability and policy. The route builds on electrical fundamentals and thermodynamics, then adds system sizing and measurement.
responsibilities: Estimate resource availability and load profiles
Size generation, storage and conversion equipment
Model performance and payback honestly, including uncertainty
Respect electrical safety and local code requirements
portfolioIdeas: A rooftop PV sizing study for a real building with measured load data
A small solar test bench with measured output versus modelled output
An energy audit report with prioritised, costed recommendations
assumptions: Policy and tariff rules are local and change; always verify current rules before designing commercially.

rows.name: Robotics engineer
rows.summary: Builds machines that sense, decide and move: mechanics, electronics, control and software together.
rows.description: Robotics is deliberately cross-disciplinary. In the graph, robotics sits downstream of mechanics, electronics and programming, and upstream of control systems and simulation projects. Students often arrive through either mechanical or electronics, then close the gap; the graph shows both routes.
responsibilities: Integrate sensors, actuators, controllers and code into one system
Model kinematics and tune control loops
Simulate before building, and test subsystems on the bench
Document wiring, interfaces and failure modes
portfolioIdeas: A line-following or obstacle-avoiding robot with a documented control loop
A ROS 2 simulation of a mobile robot navigating a known map
A sensor-fusion experiment comparing measured and modelled behaviour
assumptions: Robotics roles often expect one deep specialism plus working knowledge of the other two areas.
Hardware costs real money; simulation-first projects are accepted as valid portfolio evidence.

rows.name: Software engineer
rows.summary: Builds and maintains software systems: features, APIs, tests and the tooling around them.
rows.description: Software engineers turn requirements into working, maintainable code. Day to day that means writing features, reviewing other people’s code, designing data models and APIs, writing tests, debugging production issues, and improving how the team ships. The graph route runs from programming fundamentals and data structures through design and testing to a deployable project.
responsibilities: Implement and maintain features across a codebase
Write and maintain automated tests and review peers’ code
Debug failures using logs, debuggers and monitoring
Estimate work and communicate trade-offs to the team
portfolioIdeas: A deployed web application with tests and a CI pipeline
A small library or CLI tool published with documentation
A bug-fix or feature pull request accepted by an open-source project
assumptions: Entry requirements differ greatly between companies and countries; this graph describes common foundations, not a hiring bar.
Teamwork, communication and version control matter as much as algorithms in most junior roles.

rows.name: Surveying and geospatial engineer
rows.summary: Measures the real world precisely and turns it into spatial data other engineers can build on.
rows.description: Surveying and geospatial engineers answer where things are, how accurately that is known, and what can be decided on the strength of it. The work runs from a levelling loop on a construction site to satellite imagery and national data sets: collecting positions, carrying the right datum and projection, building and maintaining spatial data, and stating the uncertainty in everything they hand over. The constraint is that the answer is usually used to move earth, lay pipe or settle a boundary — so the accuracy statement matters as much as the measurement.
responsibilities: Design control surveys and measurement procedures against a stated accuracy requirement
Move data between reference frames and projections without losing or faking accuracy
Build and maintain spatial data — boundaries, terrain, infrastructure — with its provenance
Turn imagery and elevation data into answers a project can act on, with the limits stated
portfolioIdeas: A topographic or boundary map built from open data with datum, projection and accuracy written on it
A GNSS accuracy study comparing environments, with the error statistics and the method stated
A terrain or imagery analysis whose uncertainty section is as long as its results section
assumptions: Legal authority is separate from technical skill: in most countries only a licensed surveyor may set legal boundaries, and this path does not make you one.
Fieldwork is physical, weather-dependent and seasonal, and a large share of the job is data management and documentation rather than instruments.
typicalRoles: GIS analyst or geospatial data engineer
Spatial data specialist in construction or utilities

rows.name: Web and mobile developer
rows.summary: Builds user-facing applications for the browser and phones.
rows.description: Web and mobile developers work closest to users: layouts, state, accessibility, performance and release cycles. The route needs programming fundamentals plus a frontend or mobile specialisation and at least one shipped, accessible application.
responsibilities: Build interfaces from designs, including keyboard and screen-reader use
Manage client state and integrate APIs
Measure and improve loading performance
Ship updates and handle user-reported defects
portfolioIdeas: A responsive, accessible web application deployed publicly
An installable progressive web app with offline support
A mobile app built with a cross-platform toolchain
assumptions: Design skills are not required, but basic layout, typography and accessibility literacy are expected.

rows.name: Algorithmic complexity

rows.name: Biocompatibility

rows.name: Boolean algebra

rows.name: Chemical equilibrium

rows.name: Differential calculus

rows.name: Work, energy and power
rows.summary: Energy bookkeeping across mechanical and electrical systems.

rows.name: Energy conversion efficiency
rows.summary: Where energy goes, and why losses matter.

rows.name: Error budget

rows.name: Feedback loops

rows.name: Flow and bottlenecks

rows.name: Integral calculus

rows.name: Kirchhoff's laws
rows.summary: Conservation of charge and energy in circuits.

rows.name: Lift and drag

rows.name: Linear algebra
rows.summary: Vectors, matrices, transformations and eigenvalues.

rows.name: Material balance
rows.summary: Mass in equals mass out plus accumulation — the accounting every process calculation starts from.

rows.name: Newton's laws of motion
rows.summary: Force, mass and acceleration as the basis of mechanics.

rows.name: Ohm's law and power
rows.summary: The relationship between voltage, current and resistance.

rows.name: Overfitting and generalisation

rows.name: Physiological signals
rows.summary: What the body produces — ECG, EMG, pressure and flow waveforms — and what an instrument can recover from it.

rows.name: PID control

rows.name: Probability distributions

rows.name: Process variation

rows.name: Network protocol layers
rows.summary: Encapsulation from link layer to application layer.

rows.name: Reactor dynamics
rows.summary: How conversion and temperature move over time inside a reacting system.

rows.name: Recursion

rows.name: The relational model

rows.name: Resolution and scale

rows.name: Sensing and actuation
rows.summary: Turning physical quantities into signals and back into motion.

rows.name: Static equilibrium
rows.summary: Forces and moments balancing in a body at rest.

rows.name: Stress and strain
rows.summary: How materials deform and where they fail.

rows.name: Supervised learning
rows.summary: Learning a mapping from labelled examples.

rows.name: Tolerances and fits

rows.name: Structural analysis study
rows.summary: Analyse a truss or beam by hand and with software, then explain every difference.
rows.description: A civil portfolio project that proves you understand structural behaviour rather than trusting output. The comparison table is the deliverable.
objectives: Determine reactions and member forces by hand
Cross-check with analysis software
Explain discrepancies and state safety factors
testingIdeas: Check equilibrium of the whole structure
Vary one member and predict the effect before recomputing
extensions: Add a deflection check
Add a load-combination case
Build a scale model and load it
safetyNotes: Physical load testing must stay far below any load that could fail suddenly; never stand under a test rig.

rows.name: Designed and manufactured part
rows.summary: Take a functional part from requirement to drawing, tolerance check and a physical or printed prototype.
rows.description: Shows the full mechanical design loop, including the part everyone forgets: the tolerance stack and the manufacturability review.
objectives: Model a part parametrically in FreeCAD or OnShape
Produce a dimensioned drawing with justified tolerances
Manufacture or print a prototype and compare it with the drawing
testingIdeas: Measure the physical part and record deviations against tolerances
Change one driving dimension and confirm the drawing updates correctly
extensions: Add a finite-element check and compare with hand calculations
Design an assembly of three parts
Reduce cost by loosening a tolerance
safetyNotes: Workshop and 3D printer safety rules apply: eye protection, ventilated printing area, no reaching into moving machines.
Do not 3D print load-bearing parts for safety-critical use.

rows.name: Containerised app with CI/CD and rollback
rows.summary: A service that builds, tests, deploys and can be rolled back, with monitoring attached.
rows.description: The DevOps portfolio piece: reproducible builds, environment configuration, migrations, health checks and a documented rollback.
objectives: Containerise the application with a small, non-root image
Automate build, test and deploy on push
Add health checks, metrics and a rollback procedure
testingIdeas: Force a failing test and confirm deployment is blocked
Roll back a deployment and record the time taken
extensions: Add infrastructure as code
Add a staging environment
Add load testing with a documented baseline

rows.name: Reproducible data analysis report
rows.summary: Clean, analyse and write up a real dataset with a script anyone can re-run.
rows.description: An analyst’s core deliverable. The value is in the cleaning decisions, uncertainty and the honest answer to the original question.
objectives: Clean a messy public dataset with documented decisions
Answer three concrete questions with statistics, not impressions
Communicate findings and limitations to a non-expert
milestones: Report reviewed by one other person
testingIdeas: Re-run the analysis from raw data and confirm identical results
Check a subset by hand against the computed output
extensions: Add an interactive dashboard
Add a statistical test for one claim
Automate monthly re-runs

rows.name: Drone flight data analysis
rows.summary: Analyse flight-log data to relate control inputs to measured motion.
rows.description: Aerospace-flavoured analysis project using logs rather than hardware: estimate response characteristics, compare against a simple model, and discuss stability.
objectives: Clean and align flight-log channels
Estimate response characteristics from measured data
Compare measured behaviour with a simplified model
testingIdeas: Sensitivity-check conclusions against a different flight
Verify units on every channel before drawing conclusions
extensions: Add a simulator comparison
Add wind-disturbance analysis
Add an automated report generator
safetyNotes: Analysis of existing logs only. Drone flight requires local legal compliance, airspace checks and never flying near people.

rows.name: ECG analysis of a public dataset
rows.summary: Take one real ECG record, clean it, measure it and say honestly what the measurement can and cannot support.
rows.description: An actual biomedical signal, worked end to end on public data instead of a synthetic sine wave: baseline wander, mains interference, beat detection, heart-rate variability and the artefact that ruins the result if you ignore it. No patient, no risk and no hardware required — and the workflow is the one used in a real device pipeline.
objectives: Load a public ECG record and document its sampling rate, gain and known artefacts
Remove baseline wander and interference and show the before-and-after without hiding the damage
Detect beats, compute a heart-rate measure, and state the uncertainty in it
deliverables: A notebook or script that runs from the raw record to the final measure
A short report naming the artefacts and the filters used to remove them
A statement of what the result does and does not show clinically
milestones: Measure computed with the artefact limited stated
testingIdeas: Apply the same pipeline to a second record and check nothing silently breaks
Deliberately inject 50 Hz interference and confirm the notch filter removes it
Compare detected beat count against the annotation file shipped with the record
extensions: Add a simple arrhythmia screen and report its false-positive rate on annotated data
Port the detection step to a microcontroller and estimate its memory use
Repeat the pipeline on an EMG record and discuss what changes
safetyNotes: Recorded public data only. Never connect a homemade circuit to a person: mains-powered equipment on a human body is dangerous and requires medically rated, isolated front ends plus institutional approval.

rows.name: Engineering calculator with load calculations
rows.summary: A calculator that performs beam and circuit checks and shows its units and assumptions.
rows.description: The interesting part is not arithmetic — it is encoding assumptions, units and failure conditions so the tool cannot quietly produce a wrong answer.
objectives: Implement engineering formulas with explicit units
Validate inputs and refuse physically impossible combinations
Show the working, not just the result
testingIdeas: Compare against a hand calculation for three cases
Feed impossible inputs (negative length, zero load) and check refusal
extensions: Add a plotted output
Add saved case files
Add a second analysis type

rows.name: Gait analysis with an open musculoskeletal model
rows.summary: Simulate one movement in an open biomechanics model and quantify how much the answer depends on your assumptions.
rows.description: The body as a mechanism: scale a musculoskeletal model to a walk cycle, drive it with motion data, and inspect the joint moments it predicts. The honest part of the project is the sensitivity study — which joint, and by how much, moves the result.
objectives: Scale an open model to a subject and check it against published segment lengths
Run an inverse kinematics and inverse dynamics analysis on one movement
Quantify sensitivity to at least two assumptions, such as mass distribution or marker placement
tools: Motion capture or public motion datasets
deliverables: A working model and settings file
Plots of joint angles and moments over the cycle
A sensitivity table naming the assumptions that matter most
milestones: Analysis run on real motion data
testingIdeas: Re-run with perturbed marker positions and check the joint moment changes as expected
Compare your model output with a published dataset for a comparable movement
Check that the model is in equilibrium where it should be, rather than drifting
extensions: Compare a movement before and after a change in load or footwear
Add a simple assistive device to the model and estimate its effect on joint load
Repeat for a second subject and report inter-subject variation
safetyNotes: Simulation on public or consented motion data. If you collect your own video, obtain consent from everyone in frame, and do not ask participants to perform movements that could injure them.

rows.name: How accurate is your GNSS, really? A field study
rows.summary: Measure what your device can actually do in three environments, and explain the differences with the mechanism.
rows.description: A field study you can run with a phone or a cheap receiver. Occupy a point whose position you know, log positions over time, then repeat under open sky, tree cover and between buildings. Compute the horizontal scatter, look at the satellite geometry, and explain the differences through geometry, multipath and signal delay rather than a shrug.
objectives: Design a repeatable field procedure and log track or raw data honestly
Compute error statistics against a known or independently measured point
Explain each environment through dilution of precision, multipath and atmosphere
deliverables: A procedure somebody else could repeat, with the equipment named
Scatter plots and error statistics per environment
A written analysis separating what your method supports from what it cannot claim
milestones: Analysis written with DOP and multipath discussed
testingIdeas: Repeat one environment on another day and see whether the statistics hold
Test whether averaging a longer log reduces error, and whether it converges
Compare the recorded positions in the datums your device reports
extensions: Compare a device using a correction service against standalone positioning
Repeat with a second device and separate hardware differences from environmental ones
safetyNotes: Fieldwork: choose safe places and times, stay out of traffic, and do not obstruct anyone. Never use this study for legal boundary work — that needs a licensed surveyor and the legal framework of your country, and a phone is not a substitute.

rows.name: Graph-powered learning assistant
rows.summary: Build your own version of a prerequisite-aware study planner over a small knowledge graph.
rows.description: The most complete portfolio project in this dataset: model a domain as a graph, query it, then generate dependency-aware study plans — the same architecture GraphMentor uses.
objectives: Model a domain with nodes, relationships and stable identifiers
Write parameterised graph queries and a bounded API around them
Generate a dependency-ordered plan and explain the reasoning
deliverables: A UI or CLI that shows the plan and its reasoning
testingIdeas: Seed twice and confirm no duplicates are created
Try a malformed or cyclic prerequisite set and verify graceful handling
extensions: Add progress tracking
Add an AI explanation layer
Add alternative routes between two nodes

rows.name: Heat exchanger sizing workbook
rows.summary: Size an exchanger from a duty, a fouling allowance and a temperature programme, then check it three ways.
rows.description: One piece of equipment, done to the standard an employer would recognise: duty, log-mean temperature difference, an overall coefficient built from individual resistances, an area, and then cross-checks against a catalogue and a simulator. The interesting result is how far the answer moves when an assumption moves.
objectives: Compute the duty and temperature programme for a stated process stream
Build the overall coefficient from a resistance network including fouling factors
Report an area and geometry, plus the sensitivity to the fouling and coefficient assumptions
deliverables: A workbook with every term exposed, not only the final number
A one-page datasheet for the chosen geometry
A sensitivity table of area against fouling allowance
milestones: Overall coefficient reproduced from published correlations
Sensitivity study and independent cross-check completed
testingIdeas: Recalculate one line of the workbook by hand and confirm the spreadsheet agrees
Compare against an independent online calculator and explain any difference over 10 %
Move the fouling factor by ±50 % and report how the area responds
extensions: Add pressure drop and check it against an allowable
Replace constant properties with a property library and see what changes
Build the same exchanger in a simulator and reconcile the two answers
safetyNotes: Steady-state calculation only. If you later test a physical exchanger, hot water above 60 °C, pressurised loops and steam need supervision, a pressure-relief path and a written risk assessment.

rows.name: Home lab with monitoring and detection
rows.summary: Build small infrastructure, monitor it and write detections that produce usable alerts.
rows.description: A security or DevOps portfolio piece that shows you can operate systems: instrument, alert, triage and document.
objectives: Run two or three services in isolated virtual machines or containers
Collect metrics and logs centrally
Write three detections and document their false-positive behaviour
testingIdeas: Generate benign load and confirm alerts stay quiet
Simulate a failed login burst and confirm the detection fires
extensions: Add automated backup and restore test
Add asset inventory
Add a written runbook per service

rows.name: Kinetics fit and reactor sizing study
rows.summary: Fit a rate law to published data, then size two reactor types for the same duty and explain the difference.
rows.description: Reaction engineering done without a laboratory: published conversion-versus-time data, a fitted rate law with stated uncertainty, and then a CSTR and a plug-flow reactor sized for the same production rate. Comparing the two volumes is where the learning lands.
objectives: Fit a rate law to published data and report residuals rather than a single R² value
Derive the design equations for the chosen reactor type
Compare CSTR, plug-flow and batch volumes for an identical duty and explain the gap
deliverables: A fitting notebook or script with the data source cited
Design calculations for two reactor types
A written comparison naming the assumptions that drive the difference
milestones: Rate law fitted with residuals reported
testingIdeas: Refit with a subset of the data and report how much the parameters move
Check that the units in the rate constant are consistent with the rate law as written
Reproduce the numerical solution with a second method, such as an analytical limit case
extensions: Add temperature dependence through an Arrhenius term and discuss the extra uncertainty
Add a simple heat balance and locate the hot spot
Run the same kinetics in a kinetics library and compare the predictions
safetyNotes: Published data and simulation only. Do not attempt an exothermic reaction experiment outside a supervised laboratory with proper cooling, shielding and waste handling.

rows.name: Line balancing and layout for a small assembly
rows.summary: Design a real assembly line on paper: takt time, station content, staffing and the bottleneck.
rows.description: Choose a product you can describe with ten to thirty assembly steps — a lamp, a bike, a control panel — estimate the work content of each step honestly, and balance them into stations against a takt time derived from demand. Then state what it costs, who does what, and where the line will break first.
objectives: Break a product into work elements with realistic time estimates
Compute takt time from demand and balance the elements into stations
Design a layout, staffing level and buffer policy that can actually run
deliverables: A precedence diagram and a station balance table
A layout drawing at scale with flow direction and buffer locations
A one-page explanation of the bottleneck and your contingency for it
milestones: Work elements and times documented with sources
Balance achieved within the takt time
testingIdeas: Re-balance with a 20 % demand increase and report how many stations you must add
Check the balance against a variability assumption rather than against perfect times
Ask someone to walk your layout on paper and find where they get stuck
extensions: Add changeover between two product variants and quantify the cost
Introduce a kanban sizing rule for the buffers you designed
Redesign one station for ergonomics and re-time it
safetyNotes: A paper design exercise. If you trial it physically, the work area needs an assessment for manual handling, machine guarding and electrical risk before anyone stands in it, and the people doing the work must be involved in the design.

rows.name: Line-following robot
rows.summary: A small robot that follows a track and can be tuned for speed versus stability.
rows.description: The classic control-loop project. It combines sensors, motor driving and a control loop you can tune and measure — perfect evidence for robotics or electronics roles.
objectives: Read reflectance sensors and convert them into an error signal
Drive motors through a driver IC with PWM
Tune a proportional control loop and record the results of three tunings
deliverables: Control-loop tuning table (Kp variation, observed behaviour)
testingIdeas: Time three runs at each tuning and plot the variance
Test on a curve, a sharp corner and a broken line
extensions: Add PID with measured integral wind-up behaviour
Add obstacle detection
Add data logging of the error signal
safetyNotes: Use a battery pack with a fuse or protection board; never leave a charging battery unattended.
Keep the robot off the floor while testing with wheels spinning to avoid pinch injuries.

rows.name: Risk file for a simple assistive device
rows.summary: Design a small assistive device on paper and produce the risk documentation a reviewer would ask for.
rows.description: The part of medical engineering that is not a calculation: intended use, users and environments, hazard analysis, risk controls with evidence, and the residual risk you accept in writing. The device can be deliberately simple — a pill organiser, a walking aid, a grip attachment — because the documentation is the deliverable.
objectives: Write an intended use and user profile that excludes the cases you cannot support
Identify hazards and hazardous situations from use, misuse and foreseeable abuse
Specify risk controls and the verification evidence for each control
deliverables: A risk table: hazard, sequence of events, harm, severity, controls, verification
A short statement of residual risk and the open questions you would need a clinician to answer
milestones: Intended use and user profile written
Hazard analysis complete against a checklist
testingIdeas: Ask someone unfamiliar with the device to attempt the task and record what they did wrong
Check every control has an evidence reference, and delete any control you cannot verify
Re-read the intended use and confirm nothing in the file claims more than it allows
extensions: Add a usability test with five participants and summarise the failures
Compare your file structure against a published regulatory guidance outline
Draft the labelling and instructions for use, including the limits
safetyNotes: A documentation exercise, not a regulatory submission. Nothing in this project authorises making a medical claim or supplying a device: check the rules that apply where you live before building anything for a person to use.

rows.name: Image classifier with an honest evaluation
rows.summary: Fine-tune a vision model and report performance with an error analysis, not just accuracy.
rows.description: The deliverable that matters is the evaluation: a held-out test set, a confusion matrix, an error analysis and a statement of what the model must not be used for.
objectives: Prepare and split a dataset with no leakage
Train a baseline and a transfer-learning model
Report metrics, error analysis and limitations
deliverables: Model card with intended use and limitations
milestones: Final evaluation and model card written
testingIdeas: Verify no image from the test set appears in training
Measure performance on two subgroups to check for obvious bias
extensions: Deploy behind an API with latency measurement
Add a simple interface for testing
Quantise the model for speed

rows.name: Process flow diagram with a closed mass balance
rows.summary: Pick a real process, draw the flow diagram and prove every kilogram is accounted for.
rows.description: A complete piece of process work at the smallest honest scale: one unit on a page, a stated basis, a balance that closes, and assumptions written where a reviewer can argue with them. A flow diagram is also the artifact a hiring manager can actually read.
objectives: Choose and state the process basis: feed rate, composition and operating conditions
Draw a legible process flow diagram with stream numbers, equipment tags and utilities
Close the overall mass balance and reconcile it against a published description of the process
deliverables: A balance table with the closing error stated as a percentage
A short note listing every assumption and what would falsify it
milestones: Balance closed to within 2 %, with any residual explained
Recycle and utility streams added without breaking the balance
testingIdeas: Re-close the balance from your own table without looking at your working
Ask another person to read the diagram and tell you which stream is the feed and which is the product
Check units on every number: a row without units is a defect
extensions: Add an energy balance and size the largest heater or cooler
Enter the same flowsheet in a simulator and compare the two balances
Add the control scheme for the most important variable in the process
safetyNotes: A paper exercise on published process descriptions. Do not build or run the process: even a scaled-down version of a real flowsheet needs a supervised laboratory, a chemical hazard assessment and a relief path.

rows.name: PID temperature controller
rows.summary: Model, simulate and then build a closed-loop temperature controller with measured performance.
rows.description: The definitive control project: identify the plant, design and tune the loop, then compare simulated and measured response with numbers.
objectives: Identify a first-order plant model from step-response data
Simulate and tune a PID controller
Measure the real system’s settling time and steady-state error
testingIdeas: Apply a step setpoint change and record rise time, overshoot and settling time
Introduce a disturbance and confirm recovery
extensions: Add an anti-windup strategy
Add feed-forward control
Log data and tune automatically
safetyNotes: Keep heater power low (a few watts) and under software and hardware limits; use a thermal fuse where practical.
Never leave a powered heater unattended.

rows.name: Conveyor interlock logic, simulated
rows.summary: Write and simulate machine control logic, then argue why the safety function does not live in the software.
rows.description: Automation without a factory: a simulated conveyor with start, stop, jam detection and an emergency stop, written as ladder or state-machine logic, tested against a fault list you write yourself. The point is not the simulation — it is the reasoning about what the logic may control and what must be hard-wired.
objectives: Write control logic for a simple machine with defined states and transitions
Test the logic against a written fault list, including stuck sensors and power restoration
Set out which functions must be safety-rated hardware and why
deliverables: Simulated logic with a readable state description
A fault-injection table with the observed response for each fault
A safety rationale separating control functions from protective functions
milestones: Fault list tested and results recorded
testingIdeas: Restore power mid-cycle and confirm the machine does not restart itself
Force a sensor to stick at its last value and record what your logic does
Press emergency stop during the fastest part of the cycle and check the safe state
extensions: Add a second conveyor and an interlock between them
Add production counting and a simple efficiency calculation
Rewrite the safety function as a risk assessment with a required performance level
safetyNotes: Simulation only. Do not wire, program or interfere with a real machine control panel: that work needs lock-out/tag-out training, arc-flash protection, employer authorisation and supervision, and it kills people who improvise it.

rows.name: Personal engineering portfolio site
rows.summary: A responsive site that presents your projects, skills and contact details.
rows.description: The lowest-risk way to practise frontend fundamentals and produce something you can share immediately. The bar is not visual flair; it is accessibility, honest content and a working deployment.
objectives: Structure a page with semantic HTML and responsive CSS
Meet basic accessibility requirements (keyboard, contrast, labels)
Deploy publicly and link the repository from the site
milestones: Layout and content in place locally
Keyboard-only pass and contrast fixes completed
Deployed with a custom title and description
testingIdeas: Navigate the entire site with the keyboard only
Run an automated accessibility check and fix every serious issue
Verify at 320 px width and at 100% and 200% browser zoom
extensions: Add a project detail page per project
Add a print stylesheet so the site exports as a PDF CV
Turn it into an installable PWA

rows.name: Solar PV sizing and yield tool
rows.summary: Size a PV system and compare modelled yield against measured production.
rows.description: Combines renewable fundamentals with software and data work: resource data in, sizing out, then an honest comparison with reality including seasonal effects.
objectives: Model daily load from measured or estimated data
Size generation, inverter and battery with stated assumptions
Compare predicted and measured yield over at least one month
testingIdeas: Check the tool refuses physically impossible inputs
Sensitivity-check the result against ±20% irradiance
extensions: Add tilt and shading corrections
Add payback analysis with tariffs
Add a battery cycle-life model
safetyNotes: Design work only — do not open or modify installed PV systems; DC arcs and stored energy are lethal.
Any installation work must be done by a licensed electrician following local code.

rows.name: A real map of a place you know, from open data
rows.summary: Build a map that answers one question about your neighbourhood, with its projection and accuracy stated.
rows.description: Pick a small area — your neighbourhood, a campus, a route you use. Assemble a base map, at least one boundary layer, one point layer and one thematic layer from open data or your own field notes, put everything in one coordinate reference system on purpose, and produce a print layout at a stated scale. The map has to answer a question, not merely be colourful.
objectives: Assemble layers from at least two independent sources and record where each came from
Choose and justify a coordinate reference system for the area and the scale
Produce a legible map that answers one specific question
deliverables: A project file plus an exported map with title, scale bar, north arrow and data sources
A one-page note on the projection chosen, the accuracy of each layer, and what you could not map
A layer list with each field’s meaning and units
milestones: Source data downloaded with licences noted
Layout exported at a stated scale
testingIdeas: Overlay two data sets that should line up and measure the disagreement
Reproject the map and check that distances and areas still look sane
Ask somebody unfamiliar to read the map and tell you what it answers
extensions: Publish the same content as an interactive web map and note what the web viewer loses
Add a field-collected layer with an accuracy estimated from your own measurements
Rebuild one layer from a second source and state which is better and why
safetyNotes: Field collection: mind road traffic, weather and private property. Do not record people or enter sites without permission, and respect the licence and attribution terms of every data source you use.

rows.name: Backend API service with tests
rows.summary: A small but complete service: data model, validation, auth, tests and documentation.
rows.description: Builds the backend habits that matter: parameterised database access, layered validation, consistent errors, tests at the API boundary and honest documentation.
objectives: Design a resource model and implement CRUD endpoints
Validate all input and return consistent error bodies
Write integration tests covering the API surface
testingIdeas: Test unauthorised access returns 401 and another user’s record returns 404
Send malformed and oversized payloads and check the error shapes
extensions: Add pagination and rate limiting
Add a container build
Add a CI pipeline with a test database

rows.name: Mobile robot simulation in ROS 2
rows.summary: Simulate a differential-drive robot that maps a space and navigates to a goal.
rows.description: Robot software without hardware cost. You learn the ROS 2 node graph, transforms, sensors and navigation, and produce behaviour you can demonstrate to anyone with a screen.
objectives: Describe a robot model and simulate it in Gazebo
Publish sensor data and build an occupancy map
Navigate to a target pose and record the path and success rate
deliverables: Video or plots of five navigation runs with success rate
testingIdeas: Run navigation five times from different starts and record success
Deliberately block the path and verify replanning
extensions: Add a second robot with coordination
Add real hardware with the same interface
Add vision-based landmark detection
safetyNotes: Simulation only — no physical robot in this version. If you later deploy to hardware, isolate the battery and add an emergency stop before first motion.

rows.name: Security audit of your own project
rows.summary: Attack your own application lawfully, document the findings and fix them.
rows.description: Written permission and ownership are the point: audit something you built. The deliverable is a report with reproductions, severities, fixes and retest evidence.
objectives: Produce a threat model for your own application
Test for injection, XSS, broken access control and secret leakage
Fix and retest, documenting residual risk
testingIdeas: Verify an unauthorised user cannot read another user’s records
Confirm error responses no longer leak internal details
extensions: Add automated security checks to CI
Add dependency scanning
Add a written disclosure policy
safetyNotes: Only test systems you own or have explicit written permission to test. Unauthorised testing is a criminal offence in most countries.
Keep the lab isolated from your home network.

rows.name: Sensor data logger
rows.summary: Log temperature and humidity for a week and analyse the resulting data honestly.
rows.description: Introduces the full measurement loop: sensor, microcontroller, storage and analysis. It also teaches the difference between a reading and a measurement, which shows up as offset, noise and drift.
objectives: Read a digital sensor reliably and store timestamped readings
Recover the data and plot it
Quantify noise, drift and missing data instead of ignoring them
deliverables: A short analysis report with limitations
testingIdeas: Compare readings against a second thermometer and record the offset
Deliberately disconnect the sensor and confirm the system recovers
extensions: Add MQTT upload
Add battery power and measure runtime
Add a calibration routine
safetyNotes: Use low-voltage (3.3 V/5 V) supplies only; do not connect anything to mains power.
Disconnect power before rewiring the board.

rows.name: Change detection from satellite imagery, validated
rows.summary: Find a real change between two satellite dates — then validate it instead of asserting it.
rows.description: Pick an area and two dates either side of a change you have independent reason to expect: a construction site, a burn scar, a seasonal flood. Work with Sentinel imagery at its real resolution, mask cloud properly, compute an index or band difference, and then validate part of the result against something known. The deliverable pairs a map with an honest error discussion.
objectives: Search, download and document imagery with acquisition dates and processing level
Mask cloud and shadow and explain what that removed
Compute a change metric, then validate a sample of it against independent evidence
tools: Copernicus Data Space browser and APIs
deliverables: Before and after composites plus the change map with legend and scale
A validation table: sample points, what the map says, what the reference says, disagreements included
An uncertainty note covering resolution, registration, seasonality, and what would strengthen the result
milestones: Change metric computed and validated on a sample
testingIdeas: Repeat with a different index or threshold and report how much the answer moves
Shift one image by a pixel and check whether your result survives — registration matters
Examine a known false-positive area such as open water or bare soil and say how you would separate it
extensions: Add a third date to separate permanent change from seasonal variation
Classify the type of change rather than only detecting that it happened
Automate the pipeline so the same result can be produced from the raw archive
safetyNotes: Respect imagery licence and attribution terms, and do not publish claims about specific private sites or identifiable people. Satellite imagery can reveal sensitive locations: treat anything you can identify as personal data.

rows.name: Control chart study on a real measurement series
rows.summary: Take a real process measurement series, chart it properly and say which signals matter.
rows.description: A quality-engineering exercise with no laboratory needed: a public or self-collected measurement series, a chart chosen for the data type, control limits computed from the process rather than the specification, and a written judgement on what each out-of-control signal means — including the ones you decide are ordinary variation.
objectives: Choose the right chart for the measurement type and justify the choice
Compute control limits from the data and mark every signal against the standard rules
Separate the signals that indicate a real change from the ones you judge to be routine
deliverables: A chart with limits, signals and the rule cited for each signal
A capability calculation with its assumption on normality stated
A short written judgement on what you would investigate first on the shop floor
milestones: Investigation plan written with causes ranked
testingIdeas: Recompute limits on the first half of the data and check the second half behaves as expected
Introduce a deliberate shift into a copy of the data and confirm your rules catch it
Check whether a single outlier is driving your limits, and say what you did about it
extensions: Add an exponentially weighted moving average chart and compare its sensitivity
Design a sampling plan for the same process and cost it against full inspection
Repeat on an attribute measurement and discuss why the charts differ
safetyNotes: Analysis of existing data only. Do not intervene in a live production process to generate data: any change on a running line needs the owner’s authority, a risk assessment and a plan for what happens if the change degrades quality.

rows.name: Terrain and low-lying-ground screening from open elevation data
rows.summary: Derive slope and drainage from a real elevation model, then state in writing what the result cannot be used for.
rows.description: Download an elevation model for a catchment or town, derive slope and flow accumulation, identify low-lying ground relative to a river or coast, and produce a screening map. Then write the limitations section properly: vertical accuracy, resolution, the difference between a surface and bare earth, and the fact that this is not a hydraulic flood study.
objectives: Obtain and document an elevation data set with its resolution and stated accuracy
Derive terrain attributes and drainage lines with a method you can defend
Produce a screening map whose limits are stated in the same document
tools: QGIS with a terrain or hydrology plugin
OpenTopography or a national elevation portal
deliverables: A terrain map — hillshade, slope, flow accumulation — with sources cited
A low-lying-ground map overlaid with a water course and known assets
A limitations note explaining what a hydraulic study would add and who must sign one
testingIdeas: Change the flow-accumulation threshold and watch how the drainage network changes
Compare your screening against a documented flood event or a published flood map
Check several points against a second elevation source and report the disagreement
extensions: Add published rainfall scenarios and show the sensitivity of the result
Repeat with a lidar bare-earth model and compare it against the surface model
Automate the workflow so it reruns on a new tile without manual steps
safetyNotes: This is a screening exercise, not a flood risk assessment. Flood hazard, insurance and planning decisions need a licensed hydraulic study and the responsible authority. Do not publish the output as safety advice about anybody’s property.

rows.name: Traffic light state machine
rows.summary: A finite-state machine controlling LEDs with correct timing and fault handling.
rows.description: A deceptively simple project that teaches state machines, timing without blocking delays, and designing for a failure state (all-red when something is wrong).
objectives: Design a state diagram before coding
Implement non-blocking timing
Handle a lamp or sensor fault safely
testingIdeas: Measure cycle timing across 20 cycles
Simulate a stuck sensor and confirm safe behaviour
extensions: Add pedestrian request buttons
Add a second intersection with coordination
safetyNotes: Low-voltage only; never power a breadboard project from mains.

rows.name: Engineering unit converter CLI
rows.summary: A command-line tool that converts and sanity-checks engineering units with dimensional awareness.
rows.description: A small, complete piece of software: argument parsing, input validation, tests and documentation. Dimension checking teaches why unit errors crash real projects.
objectives: Parse and validate user input without crashing on nonsense
Represent units and detect incompatible conversions
Write unit tests covering correct and invalid cases
deliverables: A written list of supported conversions
testingIdeas: Convert a value and its inverse and check round-trip accuracy
Feed empty, huge and non-numeric input
extensions: Add a web interface
Add currency-style rate tables with units
Package it for pip

rows.name: Connected weather station
rows.summary: A solar-or-battery powered station that publishes measurements securely and survives outages.
rows.description: Adds connectivity, power budgeting and security to the sensor logger: per-device credentials, offline buffering, and measured power consumption.
objectives: Publish measurements over MQTT with per-device credentials
Buffer data during network outages and forward it later
Measure and report current consumption
testingIdeas: Disconnect the access point for two hours and verify no data loss
Measure sleep current and calculate battery life
extensions: Add a web dashboard
Add over-the-air firmware update with rollback
Add a second sensor with calibration
safetyNotes: Use a charge controller with any solar panel; never connect a panel directly to a battery.
Weatherproof enclosures must not trap heat around batteries.
