rows.name: 3D Slicer: medical image analysis platform
rows.summary: Free platform for loading, segmenting, registering and visualising medical images, with full documentation.
rows.provider: 3D Slicer open-source project (Brigham and Women’s Hospital and contributors)
rows.accessNote: Free and open source, with documentation and tutorials online. No account and no paid tier.
outcomes: Load a public medical image volume and inspect it in three planes
Segment a structure and export the result as a mesh
Script a repeatable processing pipeline instead of clicking through a session
rows.assumes: Basic anatomy orientation and comfort installing desktop software.
rows.limits: A tool rather than a course: the documentation explains features, not the clinical reasoning behind a segmentation decision.
rows.commitment: A weekend to the first segmentation.

rows.name: Adafruit Learning System
rows.summary: Large library of tested electronics tutorials with wiring diagrams and working code.
rows.accessNote: Tutorials are free and openly licensed with no account. Buying parts from the sponsor is optional; equivalent parts from anywhere work.
outcomes: Wire and program a sensor end to end from a tested guide
Understand what a breakout board does for an awkward chip
Modify the example code deliberately instead of hoping
rows.assumes: None for the beginner guides; a microcontroller makes them real.
rows.limits: Project-style tutorials around one vendor’s parts: the wiring usually transfers, the exact modules do not, and theory is light.
rows.commitment: An evening per project.

rows.name: All About Circuits: Textbook
rows.summary: Free online textbook covering DC, AC and semiconductor electronics.
rows.accessNote: Free to read online. Optional paid membership adds downloads; the textbook itself is free.
outcomes: Analyse DC and AC circuits with Ohm’s law and Kirchhoff’s laws
Work with reactive components, impedance and simple filters
Read the semiconductor chapters for diodes and transistors
rows.assumes: Algebra; the textbook deliberately avoids calculus.
rows.limits: No bench or simulation work, and semiconductor coverage is introductory — a breadboard or SPICE build is needed for intuition.
rows.commitment: A textbook year; chapters stand alone.

rows.name: APMonitor: Process Dynamics and Control
rows.summary: Course with runnable notebooks on process identification, PID tuning and model predictive control.
rows.accessNote: Course pages, notebooks and exercises are free to read and run. The paid option buys a certificate or graded credit; the free path includes neither.
outcomes: Model a first-order-plus-dead-time process and identify it from data
Tune a PID loop and describe the effect of each gain change
Set up a simple model predictive control problem and explain the constraints
rows.assumes: Basic Python and calculus; some process or instrumentation background helps.
rows.limits: Focused on dynamic control: no equipment sizing or process design, and the notation is software-flavoured rather than plant-flavoured.
rows.commitment: Weeks of part-time study rather than a full semester.

rows.name: Arduino Documentation
rows.summary: Official language reference and tutorials for microcontroller programming.
rows.accessNote: Documentation is free (CC BY-SA). Boards themselves are a hardware cost.
outcomes: Read a sensor and drive an actuator from a microcontroller
Use the language reference instead of copying sketches blindly
Wire a simple circuit without damaging it
rows.assumes: Basic electronics and some programming.
rows.limits: The Arduino toolchain and its boards. The abstraction hides registers, so this is not a route to low-level firmware work.
rows.commitment: A weekend per project family.

rows.name: Azure Architecture Center: API Design Best Practices
rows.summary: Concentrated reference on REST API design: resources, status codes, versioning and pagination.
rows.accessNote: Free documentation with no account required. The guidance is vendor-neutral in substance even though it is published by Microsoft.
outcomes: Design resource-oriented URLs and use status codes honestly
Version an API without breaking the clients already calling it
Choose between chatty and coarse endpoints on purpose
rows.assumes: HTTP basics and some backend experience.
rows.limits: REST practice only: nothing on event-driven or GraphQL APIs, and no implementation code.
rows.commitment: An hour or two; keep it open while you design.

rows.name: Battery University
rows.summary: Long-running reference on batteries: chemistries, charging, ageing and safety.
rows.accessNote: Free articles with no account. It is vendor-adjacent material, so treat product claims with suspicion and follow the numbers.
outcomes: Read a battery datasheet and know which numbers decide the design
Explain how charge termination, temperature and cycling age a cell
Estimate whether your device’s power budget is realistic at all
rows.assumes: Basic electricity.
rows.limits: Battery technology only: power-supply design, energy harvesting and the firmware that manages them are elsewhere.
rows.commitment: An afternoon; reference when choosing a cell.

rows.name: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (India)
rows.summary: Indian government material on energy efficiency, audits and appliance standards.
rows.provider: Bureau of Energy Efficiency, Government of India
rows.accessNote: Public government material, free to read. The certified energy auditor examination it describes is paid and has eligibility requirements.
outcomes: Say what an energy audit covers and who is legally allowed to certify one
Read efficiency standards and appliance labelling rules
See how industrial audits are scoped under Indian regulation
rows.assumes: Basic energy units and some thermodynamics.
rows.limits: Regulatory and programme material rather than a teaching course, and it is specific to Indian rules.
rows.commitment: Reference material; the auditor syllabus doubles as a study list.

rows.name: Cantera: chemical kinetics and reactor library
rows.summary: Open-source library for chemical kinetics, thermodynamics and transport, with Python tutorials and reactor models.
rows.accessNote: Open source under a permissive licence with full documentation; free to install and use with no account.
outcomes: Define a reaction mechanism and integrate it to get species profiles over time
Compute equilibrium compositions and compare them with kinetic results
Script a reactor model and post-process the concentration and temperature history
rows.assumes: Python and calculus; reaction kinetics at undergraduate level.
rows.limits: A library rather than a course: tutorials assume you know reactor theory, and the answer is only as good as the mechanism you supply.
rows.commitment: A few days to a first working reactor script.

rows.name: CircuitVerse
rows.summary: Browser-based digital logic simulator with community circuits to study.
rows.accessNote: Free and open source; a free account saves your circuits.
outcomes: Build and simulate combinational and sequential circuits
Read a timing diagram from a simulation you ran
Share a circuit as a link instead of asking someone to install software
rows.assumes: Boolean algebra basics, or a willingness to learn them alongside.
rows.limits: Simulation only: no synthesis, no timing closure, no hardware. It teaches logic, not FPGA engineering.
rows.commitment: Evenings per topic; open-ended practice.

rows.name: CoolProp: thermophysical property library
rows.summary: Open-source property library callable from Python, spreadsheets and C++ for hundreds of fluids.
rows.accessNote: Open source under a permissive licence: free to install and use, no account and no paid tier.
outcomes: Call a property library from a script or spreadsheet instead of typing a constant from memory
Compare two property models for the same fluid and quantify the difference
Generate a property table you can cite, with the model named
rows.assumes: Basic programming or spreadsheet use, plus an understanding of the properties themselves.
rows.limits: Properties only: it does not solve flowsheets and it does not warn you when a fluid or range falls outside the fitted region.
rows.commitment: An afternoon to the first property call; about a week to use it fluently.

rows.name: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem
rows.summary: Free Sentinel satellite imagery with a browser viewer, a search API and processing services.
rows.provider: European Commission and European Space Agency
rows.accessNote: Sentinel data is free and open with a free account for larger downloads and processing; terms of use and attribution apply. No cost, but the processing quota is not unlimited.
outcomes: Search and download Sentinel imagery for a place and date
View true colour and index bands in the browser before committing to a download
Obtain data with its acquisition date and processing level recorded
rows.assumes: Basic GIS or remote sensing vocabulary helps.
rows.limits: A data service rather than a teaching resource: it will not explain what an index means, and heavy processing belongs in a cloud environment.
rows.commitment: 3–12 h to become fluent in searching and downloading; analysis takes longer.

rows.name: Architecture Patterns with Python
rows.summary: Dependency injection, repositories, unit of work and events — applied architecture with runnable code, not theory.
rows.accessNote: Free to read online under an open licence; a print edition and a paid course also exist.
outcomes: Separate domain logic from frameworks so it can be tested without them
Introduce a repository or unit of work only where it pays for itself
Weigh monolith, events and services with evidence rather than fashion
rows.assumes: Working Python, some testing practice, and a project of your own to apply it to.
rows.limits: One language and one style of service application. It is opinionated, and the case study is deliberately small.
rows.commitment: A book: a few weeks of evenings, longer to apply.

rows.name: Learning How to Learn
rows.summary: Evidence-based study techniques: spaced repetition, retrieval practice, chunking.
rows.accessNote: Audit mode gives access to the videos and readings free; graded assignments and the certificate require payment or financial aid.
outcomes: Use spaced repetition and retrieval practice deliberately
Plan study around how memory actually works
Recognise your own procrastination triggers and interrupt them
rows.assumes: Nothing; it is about studying anything.
rows.limits: Audit mode gives the videos and readings, but graded work and the certificate are paid. The neuroscience is popular-level.
rows.commitment: Around 15 hours of video, best spread over weeks.

rows.name: CP Algorithms
rows.summary: Catalogue of algorithms and data structures with complexity analysis and pseudocode you can implement directly.
rows.accessNote: Free, open source and maintained in public. No account, no ads and nothing gated.
outcomes: Pick a data structure for a problem and justify the choice
Implement graph, string and number-theory routines from the explanations
Estimate the cost of an approach before writing it
rows.assumes: A language you can write in, plus basic complexity notation.
rows.limits: Competitive-programming framing: worst-case speed over maintainable design, and little on testing or real-system constraints.
rows.commitment: Reference; the introductory sections take a few evenings.

rows.name: The Cryptopals Crypto Challenges
rows.summary: Eight sets of hands-on challenges that break real cryptographic constructions, from XOR to padding oracles.
rows.accessNote: Free, no account, and no solutions needed to begin. Community write-ups are easy to spoil yourself with.
outcomes: Implement and then break ECB, CBC and stream cipher modes
Recognise why a padding oracle or a nonce reuse is fatal
Read a protocol specification sceptically
rows.assumes: A language you can write in and a willingness to work in bytes and hex; no prior cryptography.
rows.limits: Breaking implementations rather than designing systems: no key management, no deployment, no compliance. It is a teaching arena, not a review.
rows.commitment: Months if worked honestly; the first set is a weekend.

rows.name: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science
rows.summary: Harvard’s introduction to computer science, covering C, Python, SQL and web.
rows.accessNote: All lectures and problem sets are free; the optional verified edX certificate is paid.
outcomes: Write C, Python and SQL to solve problems rather than follow along
Reason about memory, data structures and the cost of an algorithm
Build and deploy a small web application
rows.assumes: No prior programming, but a serious appetite: the problem sets are famously demanding.
rows.limits: Hard by design and paced like a Harvard term. The paid edX certificate adds nothing the free material lacks.
rows.commitment: Roughly 100–200 hours; a full term for most learners.

rows.name: U.S. Chemical Safety Board: investigation reports
rows.summary: Public investigation reports into real process incidents, with technical and organisational findings.
rows.accessNote: Public investigation reports, free to read and reuse with attribution. No account needed.
outcomes: Read a real incident and trace its technical and organisational causes
Identify which design change would have prevented or mitigated the event
Use evidence from an incident to justify a safeguard in your own design work
rows.assumes: Enough process knowledge to follow a flowsheet and a chemistry discussion.
rows.limits: Case studies rather than instruction: they show what went wrong, not the design method that would have caught it.
rows.commitment: An hour or two per report, and the findings need reading twice.

rows.name: U.S. Chemical Safety Board: video library
rows.summary: Short animated incident reconstructions that make the sequence of a process failure visible.
rows.accessNote: Public videos, free to watch and share. No account needed.
outcomes: Watch a failure sequence step by step rather than reading it
Explain how a small deviation grew into a major incident
Use a shared example when discussing a safeguard with people who do not read reports
rows.assumes: No technical background: the reconstructions are written for a general audience.
rows.limits: Short, simplified summaries: no data, no calculations and no substitute for the full investigation report.
rows.commitment: Ten minutes per video.

rows.name: From Data to Viz
rows.summary: Decision guide for charts: which one fits your data, and how each is commonly misread.
rows.accessNote: Free decision tree and caveat pages with no account. Code examples for each chart link out to R, Python and D3.
outcomes: Pick a chart from the shape of your data rather than habit
Read the pitfalls listed for that chart type before publishing it
Find runnable code for the chart in the language you already use
rows.assumes: You already have data and a plotting tool.
rows.limits: Chart selection and pitfalls only: no statistics, no design theory, nothing about layout or accessibility.
rows.commitment: Minutes per chart decision; reference afterwards.

rows.name: Docker: Get Started
rows.summary: Official introduction to images, containers, volumes and compose.
rows.accessNote: Documentation is free. Docker Desktop has licence terms for larger organisations — check before commercial use.
outcomes: Build an image and run it as a container
Persist data with volumes and run multi-service apps with compose
Get a shell inside a running container and debug it
rows.assumes: Command-line comfort; no Kubernetes knowledge needed.
rows.limits: Docker’s own tooling: image security, registry policy and orchestration are separate topics, and Docker Desktop carries licence terms for larger organisations.
rows.commitment: A weekend to a week.

rows.name: DoITPoMS: Teaching and Learning Packages (University of Cambridge)
rows.summary: Short materials-science packages, including biomedical materials, with worked examples and interactive diagrams.
rows.provider: University of Cambridge (Department of Materials Science and Metallurgy)
rows.accessNote: Free teaching packages published by the university, no account needed.
outcomes: Work through one materials topic with diagrams, derivation and examples
Connect structure and processing to measured properties
Cover the biomedical materials packages relevant to implants and devices
rows.assumes: Undergraduate materials science or equivalent; each package states its prerequisites.
rows.limits: Short packages rather than a course, and coverage is uneven across the discipline.
rows.commitment: Two to four hours per package.

rows.name: The Scientist and Engineer’s Guide to Digital Signal Processing
rows.summary: Free online textbook on digital signal processing with unusually clear explanations of filters.
rows.accessNote: The full text is published free online by the author, chapter by chapter, with no account and no paid tier.
outcomes: Design and apply digital filters and understand what they do to a signal
Understand sampling, aliasing and the Fourier transform in practical terms
Read biomedical signal literature without being blocked by the notation
rows.assumes: Algebra and a little calculus; no prior signal processing.
rows.limits: Written with older software conventions and no modern library examples, and it stops short of adaptive and statistical signal processing.
rows.commitment: A chapter at a time; a few weeks for the parts you need.

rows.name: DWSIM open-source process simulator
rows.summary: Free steady-state process simulator with unit operations, property packages, flowsheeting and scripting.
rows.accessNote: Free and open source (GPL). Download and use at no cost, with no account and no feature gate.
outcomes: Build a flowsheet from unit operations and converge a steady-state simulation
Choose a property package and explain why that package fits the chemistry
Reconcile a simulation result against an independent hand balance
rows.assumes: Material and energy balances, and comfort installing desktop software.
rows.limits: Community-supported: examples and documentation are thinner than commercial tools, and convergence failures need interpretation rather than a message that tells you what is wrong.
rows.commitment: A weekend to the first converged flowsheet; several weeks to use it with confidence.

rows.name: U.S. Department of Energy: How Does Solar Work?
rows.summary: Plain-language explanations of PV, thermal and grid integration.
rows.accessNote: Public information, free to read. Country-specific rules differ from those described.
outcomes: Explain how photovoltaic and thermal solar work in plain language
Describe how a solar installation connects to a grid
Know which parts of a system dominate cost and complexity
rows.assumes: None; it is written for the general public.
rows.limits: US policy and incentives framing — rules differ by country — and it is an explainer, not a design guide.
rows.commitment: About an hour of reading; reference afterwards.

rows.name: ENERGY STAR: Benchmarking and Energy Management
rows.summary: The US EPA programme for measuring and improving building energy performance, including the Portfolio Manager tool.
rows.accessNote: Public guidance and a free benchmarking tool. Registering to save buildings needs an account; nothing is paid.
outcomes: Benchmark a building and interpret its score against comparable ones
Turn benchmark results into a prioritised list of measures
Track performance over time instead of trusting a single reading
rows.assumes: Basic building systems and energy units.
rows.limits: Benchmarking starts an audit; it is not one. It is US-centric and building-focused, and it does not replace a site survey or metered measurement.
rows.commitment: An afternoon per building; a programme over months.

rows.name: Engineering ToolBox
rows.summary: Reference tables and formulas for materials, fluids, heat and mechanics.
rows.accessNote: Reference pages are free to read with ads; optional paid membership removes ads and unlocks extras. Verify values against a primary source before design use.
outcomes: Look up material properties, fluid data and standard formulas
Cross-check a hand calculation against published data
Convert units without losing track of what you have
rows.assumes: Nothing; it is a lookup reference.
rows.limits: Third-party tables with no peer-review trail and no guarantee of currency — verify anything safety-critical against a primary source.
rows.commitment: Reference; no linear commitment.

rows.name: ESA Navipedia
rows.summary: A technical GNSS wiki from the European Space Agency education context: signals, ranging, errors and augmentation.
rows.accessNote: Free, openly accessible GNSS wiki maintained in the ESA education and training context; no account to read.
outcomes: Work through GNSS fundamentals with equations rather than hand-waving
Understand error sources, dilution of precision and augmentation services
Connect receiver output to the physics that produced it
rows.assumes: Undergraduate mathematics; some signal handling helps.
rows.limits: A wiki with uneven article depth and a European programme viewpoint; verify anything normative against official documentation.
rows.commitment: Reference; 10–25 h for the fundamentals.

rows.name: ESP-IDF: Low Power Mode
rows.summary: Official guide to sleep modes, power domains and wake sources on the ESP32 family, with currents for each mode.
rows.accessNote: Free and open source documentation with no account required.
outcomes: Pick a sleep mode from the power budget you have to meet
Configure wake sources — timer, GPIO, touch, ULP — deliberately
Measure and reduce the average current of a battery-powered device
rows.assumes: Embedded C and a working ESP32 toolchain; this is not a beginner tutorial.
rows.limits: One chip family, and documentation rather than teaching: analog low-power design, energy harvesting and battery selection are not covered.
rows.commitment: Days per feature, with a meter and a board in front of you.

rows.name: EU Medical Device Regulation 2017/745 (EUR-Lex)
rows.summary: The full text of the European Union medical device regulation, published on the official legal database.
rows.accessNote: Official legal text, free to read in the EU legal database. It is long and it is law, not guidance.
outcomes: Read the requirements as written rather than as summarised
Compare one requirement between two jurisdictions
Know which annexes are relevant to a device class
rows.assumes: Familiarity with regulatory concepts; the text assumes the reader knows the terminology.
rows.limits: Legal text with no explanation or worked example, and it is amended over time — always check the consolidated current version.
rows.commitment: Days to navigate usefully; it is a reference, not a read-through.

rows.name: US FDA: Device Advice — regulatory assistance for medical devices
rows.summary: The United States regulator’s own explanation of device classification, pathways and quality expectations.
rows.provider: United States Food and Drug Administration
rows.accessNote: A United States government publication, free to read with no account. It describes one country’s requirements and would need mapping to any other jurisdiction.
outcomes: Understand how devices are classified and which route each class follows
Read the regulator’s expectations for design controls and quality
Find the primary source instead of a summary blog
rows.assumes: No legal training, but the language is regulatory rather than technical.
rows.limits: United States only, procedural rather than explanatory, and it does not tell you how to engineer anything.
rows.commitment: Reference use, an hour per topic.

rows.name: Flutter Documentation
rows.summary: Google’s cross-platform toolkit in Dart, with a widget catalogue, codelabs and cookbook recipes.
rows.accessNote: Free and open source. Tooling and emulators are free; app-store accounts and iOS builds are not.
outcomes: Build a screen from widgets and manage state deliberately
Separate interface from logic well enough to test it
Ship the same application to Android, iOS, desktop and web
rows.assumes: Basic programming; Dart is introduced but object-oriented concepts are not.
rows.limits: Dart and Flutter specifically — little of it transfers to React Native — and the docs favour Google’s own packages.
rows.commitment: Days for the codelabs; weeks for a real application.

rows.name: FreeCAD Documentation
rows.summary: Manual and tutorials for parametric 3D modelling.
rows.accessNote: Wiki content is freely licensed; software is open source.
outcomes: Model parametric parts and assemble them
Produce drawings and export for manufacture or 3D printing
Script a repetitive model instead of clicking through it
rows.assumes: Nothing for the basics; engineering drawing conventions help.
rows.limits: A community wiki, so page quality varies, and release churn means some tutorials lag the software.
rows.commitment: Weeks of practice; the wiki is reference.

rows.name: freeCodeCamp: Scientific Computing with Python
rows.summary: Hands-on Python curriculum with certification projects.
rows.accessNote: Free to complete; the non-profit accepts donations but nothing is gated.
outcomes: Build small programs to a written specification, against tests
Work with strings, lists, dictionaries, classes and files
Finish five certification projects you can show someone
rows.assumes: None — it starts at variables and loops.
rows.limits: The free certificate is not a credential employers ask for; the projects you build are what carry weight.
rows.commitment: Advertised at around 300 hours; realistically several weeks part-time.

rows.name: Gazebo simulation tutorials
rows.summary: Guides for simulating robots, sensors and worlds.
rows.accessNote: Free and open source.
outcomes: Model worlds, sensors and robots for simulation
Connect a simulated robot to your control code
Iterate on a design without touching hardware
rows.assumes: ROS 2 or equivalent basics.
rows.limits: Simulation is not reality: it will not teach physical-robot debugging, and version churn breaks older tutorials.
rows.commitment: Days; reference afterwards.

rows.name: GDAL documentation
rows.summary: The command line and library that read, convert and reproject nearly every spatial format in existence.
rows.accessNote: Free, open-source documentation. GDAL ships inside QGIS and most geospatial Python stacks, so you rarely install it on its own.
outcomes: Convert, subset and reproject raster and vector data from the command line
Inspect and repair the metadata that keeps spatial data honest
Batch-process data without a GUI, and script it
rows.assumes: Comfort with a command line and file paths.
rows.limits: Reference material with a steep surface: syntax is precise and unforgiving, and the pages do not teach the concepts behind the flags.
rows.commitment: Use as needed; 5–15 h to become fluent in the formats you actually use.

rows.name: GD&T Basics: Symbols and Rules
rows.summary: Reference for geometric dimensioning and tolerancing: each symbol, what it means, and how it is commonly misread.
rows.accessNote: The reference pages are free to read. Full courses and templates are paid, and nothing on the free pages is gated.
outcomes: Read a feature control frame correctly
Tell a datum apart from a basic dimension
Explain why a position tolerance replaces a ± dimension
rows.assumes: Engineering drawings — orthographic views and dimensions.
rows.limits: A symbols-and-rules reference rather than a course, and it follows ASME convention: ISO practice differs in places.
rows.commitment: An afternoon to read; reference whenever a drawing appears.

rows.name: LibreTexts Geosciences library
rows.summary: Openly licensed textbook chapters covering physical geography, cartography and geospatial fundamentals.
rows.accessNote: Free, openly licensed textbook chapters; no account needed to read, and chapters can be reused with attribution.
outcomes: Read the physical geography behind a mapping question rather than guessing it
Find surveying and cartography fundamentals with worked examples
Check terminology against a stable textbook source
rows.assumes: None; written at undergraduate entry level.
rows.limits: A library rather than a course: depth and maintenance vary by book, and it will not teach you software.
rows.commitment: Dip in as needed; 10–30 h to cover the mapping and surveying basics.

rows.name: GeoPandas documentation
rows.summary: Scripted GIS in Python: spatial joins, overlays, reprojection and mapping without a GUI.
rows.accessNote: Free, open-source documentation under a BSD licence. Needs a working Python environment; no account.
outcomes: Load spatial files into data frames and inspect geometries and attributes
Join, clip, overlay and dissolve spatial data in reproducible code
Produce spatial analysis that can be re-run and tested instead of clicked
rows.assumes: Python and pandas basics, including installing packages.
rows.limits: Assumes its dependencies are present — installation is the usual friction — and it is silent on GIS concepts such as datums, so pair it with a conceptual source.
rows.commitment: A few evenings if you already know pandas; longer otherwise.

rows.name: GitHub Actions Documentation
rows.summary: Workflow syntax, runners, secrets handling and deployment patterns.
rows.accessNote: Free for public repositories; private repositories have a monthly minute quota. Quotas and terms can change.
outcomes: Write a workflow that builds, tests and deploys
Handle secrets without leaking them into logs
Debug a failing run from its output
rows.assumes: Git and a repository you are willing to experiment in.
rows.limits: GitHub-hosted runners specifically, with minute quotas on private repositories. Runners are not general-purpose compute.
rows.commitment: Days to a first pipeline; reference afterwards.

rows.name: GitHub Student Developer Pack
rows.summary: Free developer tools and credits for verified students.
rows.accessNote: Free but requires verified student status and a GitHub account. Benefits and partners change over time.
outcomes: Claim free or discounted developer tools while you are a student
Use cloud credits for projects that would otherwise cost money
Know what verification requires before you apply
rows.assumes: Verified student status and a GitHub account.
rows.limits: Not a learning resource: partners and benefits change, and the offer ends when you graduate.
rows.commitment: An application, not a course.

rows.name: GitLab CI/CD Documentation
rows.summary: Reference for pipelines with stages, caching, artefacts and environments.
rows.accessNote: Documentation is free and open. GitLab’s SaaS has a free tier with compute-minute quotas, and the software can be self-hosted at no licence cost.
outcomes: Write a pipeline with stages, caching and artefacts that actually help
Decide what should block a merge and what should only warn
Debug a failing job from its log rather than re-running it blindly
rows.assumes: Git and a project you can experiment in.
rows.limits: GitLab’s model: GitHub Actions and Jenkins differ in vocabulary, and deployment strategy and rollback are separate subjects.
rows.commitment: Days to a pipeline you trust.

rows.name: Global Solar Atlas
rows.summary: World Bank map and dataset of solar resource for any location.
rows.accessNote: The map, the numbers and the downloads are free with no account. The same provider sells commercial datasets and reports separately.
outcomes: Read irradiance and PV potential for a location from the map
Compare candidate sites with numbers instead of impressions
Download the underlying data and cite it properly
rows.assumes: Basic PV vocabulary.
rows.limits: Resource data rather than design: it says how much sun a place gets, not how to size or wire a system, and modelled data carries uncertainty the map does not show.
rows.commitment: Minutes per site; reference afterwards.

rows.name: Google Cloud Training
rows.summary: Free courses and labs on cloud fundamentals.
rows.accessNote: Training is free and some labs run free of charge with a free account. Resources you create beyond the free tier cost money, so set a budget alert.
outcomes: Explain core compute, storage and networking services by what they do
Follow a hands-on lab within the free tier without being billed
Notice where the free tier ends before the invoice does
rows.assumes: Command-line comfort helps; the fundamentals tracks start from zero.
rows.limits: Google Cloud’s services specifically: the concepts transfer, the product names do not, and free-tier terms change without notice.
rows.commitment: Hours per module; a fundamentals path over weeks.

rows.name: Google Machine Learning Crash Course
rows.summary: Structured introduction to ML concepts with interactive exercises.
rows.accessNote: Free; no account required for the reading, interactive exercises may need a Google account.
outcomes: Use the vocabulary correctly: features, labels, loss, generalisation
Train and evaluate a model in the interactive exercises
Spot overfitting and data problems from the curves
rows.assumes: Algebra; the course deliberately keeps calculus and programming depth out of the way.
rows.limits: An introduction with no production concerns — deployment, monitoring, drift — and it leans on Google’s own tooling.
rows.commitment: A weekend of focused work.

rows.name: GPS.gov: official information about the GPS constellation
rows.summary: Plain-language and official statements about how satellite positioning works, what accuracy is promised and what can degrade it.
rows.accessNote: A public information site with no cost and no account: policy, performance data and explanations written to be read by anyone.
outcomes: Understand what the constellation provides and what is committed publicly
Read official accuracy and availability statements rather than marketing claims
Understand interference, jamming and service degradation
rows.assumes: None beyond basic computer literacy; the pages are written for a general reader.
rows.limits: United States policy framing: the site explains the system rather than teaching you to survey with it, and other constellations have their own documentation.
rows.commitment: A few hours for the parts that matter to you.

rows.name: UK HSE: Musculoskeletal disorders
rows.summary: Regulator guidance and assessment tools for manual handling and upper-limb disorders.
rows.provider: United Kingdom Health and Safety Executive
rows.accessNote: Free government guidance with published assessment tools; no account needed.
outcomes: Use a published assessment tool rather than an opinion to judge a lifting task
Understand the legal duty to assess manual handling
Record an assessment that a reviewer would accept
rows.assumes: No technical background, though the assessment tools need care to apply.
rows.limits: United Kingdom framing, and assessment tools are screening instruments rather than a full ergonomics analysis.
rows.commitment: An afternoon to learn one tool.

rows.name: IAEA Human Health Campus
rows.summary: International Atomic Energy Agency learning material on medical imaging physics and radiotherapy.
rows.accessNote: Public educational material from an international agency, free to read. Some courses require registration for a certificate.
outcomes: Read authoritative material on imaging physics, dose and quality assurance
Understand radiation dose as a design constraint, not an afterthought
Find the international guidance that national rules usually follow
rows.assumes: Physics at undergraduate level and some familiarity with medical imaging.
rows.limits: Aimed at clinical and regulatory professionals: dense, and organised around practice rather than learning paths.
rows.commitment: Reference use; modules take hours each.

rows.name: Interactive Linear Algebra
rows.summary: Open textbook built around in-browser demos of vectors and matrices.
rows.accessNote: Free open textbook with interactive demos that run in the browser. No account required.
outcomes: See a matrix as a transformation rather than a grid of numbers
Compute eigenvalues and eigenvectors with a feel for what they mean
Connect span, rank and solvability to a problem you can state
rows.assumes: High-school algebra.
rows.limits: A first course: numerical stability, proofs depth and specialist applications are out of scope.
rows.commitment: A semester; the chapters are self-contained.

rows.name: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
rows.summary: Statistical learning from regression and classification through trees and SVMs to unsupervised methods, with labs.
rows.accessNote: The book and its lab code are free from the authors’ site. No account and no paid tier.
outcomes: Fit, validate and compare regression, classification and tree models
Choose properly between resampling, regularisation and model selection
Read a model’s output and state its uncertainty instead of a single number
rows.assumes: Linear algebra and some probability; the labs expect R or Python.
rows.limits: Classical interpretable methods: deep learning is deliberately excluded and the mathematics stays applied.
rows.commitment: Course length: a term at a chapter a week.

rows.name: Khan Academy: Human anatomy and physiology
rows.summary: Video and practice sequence on body systems, with quizzes after each unit.
rows.accessNote: Free of charge; a free account is needed to keep progress. No paid tier is required.
outcomes: Get oriented in the anatomy and physiology relevant to a device or model
Check your understanding with graded practice questions
Pick up the vocabulary you need to read clinical material
rows.assumes: School biology.
rows.limits: Introductory and largely descriptive: no engineering analysis, no measurements and no clinical detail.
rows.commitment: Ten to twenty minutes per topic.

rows.name: Khan Academy: Calculus
rows.summary: Full calculus course with practice exercises and worked solutions.
rows.accessNote: Entirely free; a free account keeps progress. No paid tier is required.
outcomes: Differentiate and integrate the standard function families
Set up related-rates and optimisation problems from a word problem
Read a limit statement and say precisely what it claims
rows.assumes: School algebra, functions and trigonometry.
rows.limits: Single-variable only — no multivariable or vector calculus. Practice is machine-graded, so nobody comments on your method.
rows.commitment: Self-paced; roughly a semester of material worked steadily.

rows.name: Khan Academy: Physics
rows.summary: Mechanics, waves and electricity with interactive practice.
rows.accessNote: Entirely free with a free account.
outcomes: Apply Newton’s laws to a body and account for every force on it
Use energy and momentum to solve problems that forces alone make awkward
Read motion from position, velocity and acceleration graphs
rows.assumes: Algebra and basic trigonometry; most units need no calculus.
rows.limits: No calculus-based treatment and no laboratory work: it is conceptual physics and problem practice.
rows.commitment: Self-paced; about a year of introductory physics if worked as a course.

rows.name: KiCad Documentation
rows.summary: Schematic capture and PCB layout documentation for the open-source EDA suite.
rows.accessNote: Free and open source.
outcomes: Draw a schematic and run electrical rule checks on it
Lay out a two-layer board and generate the files a fab needs
Understand footprints, nets and design rules
rows.assumes: Circuit theory basics; assembly knowledge is not assumed.
rows.limits: Tool documentation, not electronics theory, and manufacturing or assembly constraints get only light coverage.
rows.commitment: A project or two to become fluent.

rows.name: Kubernetes Tutorials
rows.summary: Official walkthroughs for pods, deployments, services and configuration.
rows.accessNote: Free documentation; running a cluster locally needs no cloud account.
outcomes: Deploy an application and expose it with a service
Configure workloads with ConfigMaps and secrets
Read pod status, events and logs to find a failure
rows.assumes: Containers (Docker) and YAML.
rows.limits: The API surface, not running production clusters: upgrades, cost control and networking are advanced material elsewhere.
rows.commitment: Days per topic; a cluster project to consolidate.

rows.name: Esri Learn: free tutorials and courses
rows.summary: Vendor-maintained tutorials that teach GIS workflows with ready-made data and a clear sequence.
rows.accessNote: Many tutorials are free; some need a free ArcGIS account, and the platform is a commercial product with metered services beyond the free tier. The concepts transfer to any GIS.
outcomes: Follow structured tutorials with data supplied and results to compare against
Practise analysis workflows end to end without assembling data first
See how a commercial GIS organises the same concepts you meet elsewhere
rows.assumes: None beyond basic computer literacy.
rows.limits: Vendor-oriented: terminology and workflows follow one product, and parts of the free path lead toward paid services.
rows.commitment: Each tutorial 1–5 h; a coherent path 15–30 h.

rows.name: LearnChemE: Chemical engineering screencasts and exercises
rows.summary: Short screencasts and self-check exercises for balances, thermodynamics, transport, separations and reactors.
rows.accessNote: Free to watch with no account. Materials are shared for teaching use under non-commercial terms, so check the licence before reusing slides.
outcomes: Work through one concept in ten minutes, then test it with the matching exercise
See worked solutions for balance, thermodynamics and separation problems
Look up a topic by course name when you already know which idea is missing
rows.assumes: Course-level chemistry and algebra; each screencast states its own prerequisites.
rows.limits: Screencasts are single-concept and short: there is no graded feedback beyond the exercises, and no design or project work.
rows.commitment: Ten minutes per screencast; a semester course is roughly 60–120 of them if worked in step.

rows.name: LibreTexts: Chemical Engineering bookshelf
rows.summary: Openly licensed textbooks covering balances, transport, separations and process control.
rows.accessNote: Openly licensed material, free to read and reuse with attribution. No account needed.
outcomes: Read a full undergraduate text on balances, transport, separations or process control
Follow worked examples with published solutions rather than statement-only problem sets
Pull one chapter for a single topic when a course elsewhere moves too fast
rows.assumes: Calculus and first-year chemistry; each book states its own starting point.
rows.limits: Depth varies between books because different authors wrote them, and there is no course structure or assessment around the shelf.
rows.commitment: Chapter by chapter; one full text is a semester of reading.

rows.name: LibreTexts: Chemical Process Dynamics and Controls
rows.summary: Open textbook on process control written from a chemical engineering perspective.
rows.provider: LibreTexts (originally University of Michigan course material)
rows.accessNote: Openly licensed (CC BY-NC-SA), free to read and reuse with attribution.
outcomes: Read process control from a process engineering perspective rather than a pure mathematics one
Trace a control loop and predict its qualitative response to a disturbance
Work through examples on sensors, control valves and controller tuning
rows.assumes: Material and energy balances and ordinary differential equations.
rows.limits: Written largely by students in its original edition and uneven in places, with occasional gaps and dated software references.
rows.commitment: A chapter at a time; the full text is a one-semester course.

rows.name: Linux From Scratch
rows.summary: Build a working Linux system from source, package by package, and in doing so learn what a distribution actually is.
rows.provider: Gerard Beekmans and the LFS community
rows.accessNote: Free to read online under an open licence; a printed copy is optional.
outcomes: Explain what a bootloader, toolchain and init actually do
Compile, patch and install packages in a dependency-correct order
Debug a build failure instead of reinstalling
rows.assumes: Comfort at a Linux shell and patience for long builds; a spare machine or virtual machine is strongly advised.
rows.limits: By design a minimal command-line system: no desktop, no package manager, no hardening. A learning exercise, not a daily driver.
rows.commitment: Days of build time, spread over weeks.
